transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve just had this down, heavy feeling for a long time. Most days I feel kind of flat or empty, even when work is going alright or people are being nice to me. It just doesn’t really lift.
How long have you been feeling this way most days?
It’s been about two years… a little over that, maybe two years and two months. It started around when that dashboard project at work put me more in the spotlight.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, socializing, or even things you previously found meaningful?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear loss of interest exactly… I still do some of the same things. They just don’t always feel like much, if that makes sense.
Have you felt more fatigued or a lack of energy most days, even if you’re not particularly busy or active?

Yeah. By the afternoon I’m usually really wiped out, even on days that aren’t that busy. Stuff that should be simple, like fixing a spreadsheet error or finishing expense paperwork, feels like I’m dragging my body and my brain through mud. Even getting myself to soccer can feel like a lot.
Have you had trouble sleeping through the night or found yourself sleeping much more than usual lately?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change like sleeping way more, and I don’t know if I’d say I’m up all night either. My sleep just feels kind of… normal enough, I guess.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over this time period?
I haven’t really noticed anything significant there. My appetite seems about the same, and I don’t think my weight has changed much.
Would you say that your depressed mood is present most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, I would say that. It’s not always intense, but most days there’s this flat, heavy feeling that kind of follows me around. Even if work is going okay or people are being nice, I still feel down or empty for a lot of the day.
Would you say that your down or heavy mood has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for the entire time you've been feeling this way?

Yeah. It’s been pretty much most days for the whole time. I’d say it started around two years and a couple months ago, when that dashboard project at work put me in the spotlight, and it’s kind of stayed with me since then.
Have you found yourself feeling worthless or guilty about things more often, even when it might not make sense logically?

Yeah, I do. A lot of it is around work. Like when people still bring up that dashboard I built, instead of just feeling good about it, my first thought is that I somehow fooled them. And then if I miss a follow-up or send an email late, it feels like proof that I’m not really as capable as they think I am.
Have you had episodes of depression like this before, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way for an extended period?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve had anything that felt this long before, at least not that I can clearly remember. I’ve had rough patches, but this feels like the first time it’s really stayed around for an extended period.
Can you recall if you’ve ever had a period of time before this one where you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I don’t really remember a clear stretch like that before this. I mean, I’ve had times where I was stressed or in a bad mood, but I can’t say there was a period where it was most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks.
Can you recall if you’ve ever had a time before this current period when you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, for more than just a few days—maybe a week or more?

I’m not sure. I don’t really have a clear memory of a time before this where it lasted like that. I’ve had bad days or a few rough stretches, but I can’t say for sure it was most of the day, nearly every day, for a week or more.
Can you think back and recall if there was ever a time before this current period when you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I really can’t think of a specific time before this where it was like that for two full weeks. I’ve had bad periods, but I don’t remember it being most of the day, nearly every day like you’re asking.

Can you recall if there was ever a time before this current period when you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks without it being due to a specific event like a loss or stress at work?

I don’t really remember an earlier separate period like that. What I can say is that for a long time now I’ve had this flat, heavy feeling most days, even when nothing specific happened—like work is fine or people are being nice—and I still just feel down and kind of empty.
Before this current period, can you recall if you ever had a time when you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, for even a week or more, even if it didn’t last as long as this one?

I still can’t really point to a separate earlier time like that. It’s more that for a long time now I’ve just been carrying this flat, heavy feeling most days. Even when work is going okay or people are being nice, I still feel down and kind of empty.
Before this current period, can you recall ever having a time when you felt down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

I don’t think so. I’m having trouble separating out a clear “before” period like that. I can’t recall a specific two-week stretch where I was down or not interested in things most of the day, nearly every day, before what’s been going on now.
Before this current period, can you recall ever having a time when you felt down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?
I don’t really have a clear memory of that happening before this. I mean, I’ve been trying to think of a separate two-week stretch like that, but nothing specific comes to mind.
